title: Custom domains, certificates and TLS for App Service
learningObjective: Map custom domains to App Service with the right DNS records and verification, and secure them with the right certificate type and TLS settings.
foundation: Every web app gets a free name like app-contoso.azurewebsites.net. To use www.contoso.com you add DNS records and prove you own the domain.
To serve https:// on your own domain you need a TLS certificate bound to the app. App Service can issue a free managed certificate for many cases.
engineer: DNS mapping: subdomains (www) use a CNAME to <app>.azurewebsites.net. The apex (contoso.com) uses an A record to the app's inbound IP (or an alias record in Azure DNS). Domain verification uses a TXT record asuid.<subdomain> (asuid for the apex) containing the app's custom domain verification ID. Custom domains require Shared tier or higher; TLS bindings require Basic or higher.

Certificates: App Service managed certificate (free, auto-renewing, no wildcard, not exportable); import from Key Vault (the app needs access to the vault; renewals sync automatically); upload a PFX (password-protected, includes the private key, at least 2048-bit RSA); App Service Certificate (purchased, stored in Key Vault).

Bindings: SNI SSL (standard) or IP-based SSL (dedicated IP). Enable HTTPS Only to redirect HTTP, and set the minimum TLS version (1.2 recommended). End-to-end TLS through Front Door or Application Gateway may need certificates there too.
Troubleshoot with nslookup/dig for CNAME/A/TXT, and remember DNS propagation and TTL.

animation.caption: Open 'Custom domain + TLS': choose records, verification and certificates for subdomain, apex and wildcard hosts.

nodes.label: DNS: CNAME www → app-contoso.azurewebsites.net, TXT asuid.www

example.title: Launching www and apex
body: www.contoso.com gets a CNAME and asuid.www TXT record and a free managed certificate. The apex contoso.com uses an A record to the app's IP and a TXT asuid record; HTTPS Only redirects HTTP traffic.
A future *.contoso.com requirement is met with a wildcard certificate imported from Key Vault, because managed certificates do not support wildcards.

prerequisites: Basic tier or higher for TLS
permissions: DNS Zone Contributor (Azure DNS) or registrar access
Key Vault Secrets User for the app's identity (Key Vault certs)
limits: Managed certificates: no wildcard, not exportable
PFX must include the private key
portal: Web app > Custom domains > Add custom domain: choose hostname record type, copy the A/CNAME and TXT values, validate, add.
Web app > Certificates: create managed certificate, import from Key Vault, or upload PFX.
Configuration > General settings: HTTPS Only, minimum TLS version.
configuration.cli:
az webapp show -g rg-web -n app-contoso --query customDomainVerificationId -o tsv
az network dns record-set cname set-record -g rg-dns -z contoso.com -n www -c app-contoso.azurewebsites.net
az network dns record-set txt add-record -g rg-dns -z contoso.com -n asuid.www -v <verification-id>
az webapp config hostname add -g rg-web --webapp-name app-contoso --hostname www.contoso.com
az webapp config ssl create -g rg-web -n app-contoso --hostname www.contoso.com
az webapp config ssl bind -g rg-web -n app-contoso --certificate-thumbprint <thumbprint> --ssl-type SNI
az webapp update -g rg-web -n app-contoso --https-only true
az webapp config set -g rg-web -n app-contoso --min-tls-version 1.2
configuration.powershell:
New-AzWebAppSSLBinding -ResourceGroupName rg-web -WebAppName app-contoso -Name www.contoso.com -CertificateFilePath .\www.pfx -CertificatePassword (Read-Host -AsSecureString) -SslState SniEnabled
Set-AzWebApp -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name app-contoso -HttpsOnly $true -HostNames @('www.contoso.com','app-contoso.azurewebsites.net')

lab.objective: Map and secure subdomain, apex and wildcard hostnames.
steps: Run the default (www, CNAME, TXT, managed cert).
Apply 'Apex with CNAME' and fix the record type.
Apply 'Wildcard with free certificate' and fix the certificate.
expected: Apex needs an A (or alias) record
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: TXT asuid record missing/incorrect or not yet propagated.
troubleshooting.fix: Check with nslookup -type=TXT asuid.www.contoso.com and wait for TTL.

troubleshooting.cause: No binding for that hostname, or certificate does not match.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an SNI binding with a matching certificate.
Use Key Vault or upload a wildcard PFX.

troubleshooting.cause: No private key, weak key or wrong password.
troubleshooting.fix: Export the PFX with private key and password, RSA ≥ 2048.

comparisons.difference: Front Door can terminate TLS and manage certificates at the edge for apps behind it.
ACM issues free certificates for AWS endpoints.

misconceptions.myth: A CNAME works at the zone apex.
misconceptions.reality: DNS does not allow a CNAME at the apex; use A or alias records.

misconceptions.myth: Free managed certificates can be exported.

architectureDecisions: Use managed certificates for simple hostnames, Key Vault for wildcards and central rotation.
Always enable HTTPS Only and TLS 1.2.

walkthrough.subtitle: Put your own domain name on a web app and serve it securely over HTTPS.
learn: DNS records for a custom domain

steps.label: Ugly URL
steps.title: Customers see app-xyz.azurewebsites.net
body: You want www.contoso.com, with a padlock in the browser.

steps.label: DNS
steps.title: Point the name at the app
body: For a subdomain (www): a CNAME record to the app's default domain. For the root domain (contoso.com): an A record to the app's IP address.
Azure also asks for a TXT record named asuid.<subdomain> with a verification ID, to prove you own the domain.

callout.text: Custom domains work from the Shared tier; TLS bindings and free managed certificates need Basic or higher.

steps.label: Certificates
steps.title: Get a certificate
body: Options: a free App Service managed certificate (Basic+, no wildcards), an App Service certificate you buy, a certificate imported from Key Vault, or uploading your own .pfx file.

steps.label: Binding
steps.title: Bind it, and force HTTPS
body: Add a TLS/SSL binding: SNI SSL (normal) or IP-based SSL. Then turn on HTTPS Only and set the minimum TLS version (1.2 or higher).

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Custom domains
recap: CNAME for subdomains, A record for the root
Managed cert (free, no wildcard), Key Vault, upload or buy
SNI binding; HTTPS Only; minimum TLS 1.2

handsOn.title: Find the domain and TLS settings and force HTTPS
handsOn.cost: Free on the F1 tier. Mapping a real domain needs a domain you own and the Basic tier (billed hourly).
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A web app on a Free plan (from the App Service plans lab).

steps.do: Open the web app > Settings > Configuration > General settings (or Settings > Configuration).
steps.see: HTTPS Only and Minimum Inbound TLS Version settings. Turn HTTPS Only On and set minimum TLS 1.2. Save.
The browser is redirected to https://.

steps.do: Open Settings > Custom domains > + Add custom domain.
steps.see: On Free tier, a message that custom domains need a higher tier. On Basic+, you would see the Domain provider, TLS/SSL certificate and Domain fields.

steps.do: Read the Custom domains page: note the 'Custom Domain Verification ID'.
steps.see: The value you would put in the TXT asuid record.
Tabs for managed certificates, bring your own certificate (.pfx) and public key certificates.

steps.do: Optional, if you own a domain and accept Basic B1 charges for an hour: scale the plan to B1, add the CNAME and TXT records at your DNS host, add the custom domain with an App Service managed certificate.
steps.see: Your domain served over HTTPS. Scale back to F1 or delete afterwards.

check: HTTPS Only is on and you located the verification ID and certificate options.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
